---
title: "Resources: The AABB quality system at a glance"
order: 14
---

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's own page on the QSE framework: origin (1997, Association Bulletin #97-04, 10
  elements), the 2023 template update, and why every current AABB Standard is built on it.
  (AABB's older URL for this same page, `.../quality/quality-systems-essentials`, now
  redirects here.) Doesn't list the ten chapter titles itself, but it's the primary source
  for the framework's existence and history — start here before citing anything about "the
  QSEs" in a real document.

- **[AABB: Standards & Accreditation](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards)**
  — AABB's general overview of its Standards and accreditation program, useful context for
  how the QSE-structured Standards relate to the accreditation relationship itself; already
  linked from the `regulatory-landscape-orientation` foundation lesson.

- **[21 CFR 606.100 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.100)**
  — the regulation containing 606.100(d), the one place FDA's own text names AABB
  directly. Use this as a stable, citable mirror of the same text quoted in the lesson;
  the local verbatim copy used for this lesson lives at `sources/cfr/606.100.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations collection](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the U.S. Government Publishing Office's official CFR collection, useful as a fallback
  primary source if a specific eCFR page is ever unreachable, and for pulling an official
  PDF of a full CFR part when you need one for the record.

- **[046: Top 5 Changes in the NEW AABB Standards with Pat
  Ooley](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6TRJwvdU6d0)** (Blood Bank Guy (D. Joe Chaffin MD),
  from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. Blood Bank Guy is a real
  transfusion-medicine educational podcast run by Dr. D. Joe Chaffin, a transfusion medicine
  educator at Loma Linda University; AABB itself partners with the channel and offers CE
  credit for episodes (see `aabb.org/bbguy`). This specific episode discusses AABB Standards
  changes directly with a guest — it won't name the QSE framework by that exact term or
  mention Lakeshore, but it's a genuinely authoritative, AABB-credentialed voice on exactly
  the point this lesson makes about QSE wording drifting edition to edition. Verified
  embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[BSI: ISO 9001 Certification — A Path to Improved
  Quality](https://www.bsigroup.com/en-US/products-and-services/standards/iso-9001-quality-management-systems/)**
  — a quality-management-standards body's own explainer on ISO 9001 generally, the standard
  this lesson uses as the strongest version of the AABB/ITIL bridge. Useful for seeing ISO
  9001's own clause structure described directly, independent of this lesson's blood-industry
  framing. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200, after a redirect to BSI's
  current URL for the page).

- **[ITSM.tools: ITIL 4 Service Value Chain — Model, Activities, and
  Examples](https://itsm.tools/itil-4-service-value-chain/)** — a well-regarded ITSM
  publication's walkthrough of the ITIL service value chain and practices this lesson invokes
  as the other half of the AABB/ITIL bridge (change enablement, incident management, problem
  management, and the rest). Useful if any of those practice names feel rusty before you map
  them onto a QSE. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[Wikipedia: ISO/IEC 20000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_20000)** — background on
  the IT service management standard this lesson pairs with ISO 9001 under the shared
  "Annex SL" harmonized clause structure (context, leadership, planning, support, operation,
  performance evaluation, improvement) used across multiple ISO management-system standards.
  Use this to see that harmonized structure described directly, rather than taking this
  lesson's word for it. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
